name: Gunsmith

google_prefill.phone: [G] the listed phone (stays the business's; customers use Rosie's one number)

A.flow: A: the customer comes to the business (video or phone count as A)

services.name: Trigger and action work
services.story: The main story: a pistol that jams. Only the $40 diagnosis is promised. Gene's written estimate is OK'd before any work, the part is ordered, and Alex pays at the counter at pick-up, with the same photo ID.

services.name: Pistol cleaning
services.story: A $50 pistol cleaning from the shop's board. Nothing is taken: a YES books the drop-off. Alex pays at the counter at pick-up.

services.name: Trigger and action work
services.story: The same repair, with the bill texted when it is ready, so Alex can pay before pick-up. The firearm is still handed back only to Alex, with the ID.

services.name: Refinish
services.story: A $250 refinish: a $125 deposit at booking, credited to the bill, and the $125 rest at the counter at pick-up.

B.flow: B: the business goes to the customer

services.name: Collection appraisal
services.story: The main story: a collection appraisal at Alex's home, up to 2 hours, $244 with the $89 trip fee in it. A card is saved for the trip fee, charged at DONE for the appraisal, and for the fee only on Sam's yes after a late cancel or a no-show. No firearm leaves the home.

services.name: Estate appraisal
services.story: An estate collection, priced at the visit after counting the firearms. A card is saved for the $89 trip fee, and Rosie texts the bill after DONE. The executor is there with the papers.

services_shape: drop-off: a firearm left at the counter unloaded and cased, checked in with a photo ID and logged, worked on, then READY and picked up only by the person who left it, with the same ID; small jobs while the owner waits; collection appraisals at the owner's home (the firearms never leave the home)
questions_before_times: the kind of firearm (pistol, revolver, rifle, shotgun) and what it needs (cleaning, a repair, a scope, a refinish, an appraisal)
whether it's an item regulated under the National Firearms Act (a suppressor, a short barrel, fully automatic): it decides whether the shop can take it
for an appraisal: how many firearms, and the town
safety_stop: someone threatening to hurt themselves or others, or someone hurt by a firearm right now
first_steps: Registration paper for a regulated (NFA) item
license: a federal firearms license that covers gunsmithing wherever the shop takes firearms in to work on them (a generic federal switch; work that federal rules count as manufacturing needs the matching license); any state or local dealer or gunsmith license where the state's rules require one; work on items regulated under the federal National Firearms Act (suppressors, short-barreled rifles and shotguns, machine guns) only where the shop's federal license and its special tax status allow it; a business registration
staff_skills: cleaning, general repair, action and trigger work, optics, barrel work, refinish, appraisal, regulated (NFA) work only with the status
messages_never: a firearm's make, model and serial number, the customer's ID details, registration papers and anything about who may lawfully have a firearm never go in a text: only on the secure page; READY and pick-up texts say 'your item'; the owner may pick a plain display name
demo_note: Demo data for testing only. [G] = prefilled from the business's Google listing at sign-up; the owner checks each field.
